newsitem.title: USA: Host Marriott deal seen beneficial.
newsitem.headline: Host Marriott deal seen beneficial.

text.p: Marriott International Inc's agreement to sell its assisted living communities to Host Marriott Corp, though fair for both parties, is especially beneficial to Host Marriott, analysts said.
"It's a fair deal for both parties and sits well with the underlying strategy of both companies," said Joyce Minor, an analyst with Lehman Brothers.
"This is the first time that Host Marriott has gone into real estate associated with assisted living facilities, which have great demographics. It provides diversification," she said.
On Tuesday Host Marriott Corp said it agreed to buy 29 senior living communities from Marriott International for $433 million and spend $107 million expanding the facilities.

"They're buying it at an attractive multiple of about eight times 1997 EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization), but Host Marriott trades at 11 to 12 times 1997 EBITDA. So while it's consistent with pricing they make for acquisitions in the hotel industry, it's a good deal for shareholders," Minor added.
Mike Mueller, an analyst with Montgomery Securities, agreed.
"I think it's a good transaction for both parties. Host acquired the properties at an attractive price," Mueller said.
"It's a great diversification move for Host because of the rapid growth of the senior living services industry, which is about 20 percent," he said.
Host Marriott's current holdings are in hotel and lodging properties.
As for Marriott International, the consensus was that the move is in line with the company's strategy of managing properties, rather than owning the real estate.
"For Marriott International, this is pretty much in line with what we have expected them to do," said Camille Humphries of Alex. Brown Securities. "We are not surprised at all."
